interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was significantly elevated at 86. The surgical findings included a pathological stage pT4b, positive surgical margins, invasion of the seminal vesicles, and the presence of lymph node metastasis. The biopsy revealed a higher grade (Gleason 4+4) compared to the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+3). The presence of lymph node metastasis is a significant adverse factor.

Countervailing findings include the absence of lymphovascular invasion and the absence of lymph node metastasis in the biopsy, although the surgical report documented nodal metastasis. The extent of extraprostatic extension and positive margins are concerning. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data widens the uncertainty regarding the subsequent trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent changes would be crucial in revising this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 30.87 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 24.70–37.05 months; its coverage has not been validated.
